facts.quote:
The Global South is disproportionately exposed 
due to structural vulnerabilities.
facts.summary: The preliminary report identifies reliance on foreign software, limited resilience and mitigation capacity, and local data gaps as structural sources of unequal exposure; it also notes disproportionate environmental and socioeconomic impacts in the global South.

facts.quote:
questions surrounding model access controls, vulnerability disclosure norms, and the 
equitable deployment of AI tools, particularly in developing economies, are increasingly becoming matters 
of international policy
facts.summary: The report frames access to defensive AI capabilities and vulnerability disclosure as international governance and equity issues, noting that developers' restricted releases concentrate safety and access decisions within a select coalition.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of reported capability restrictions; not an adopted international access regime.

facts.quote:
Transparency and accountability are key 
pillars for meaningful access to justice.
facts.summary: The report identifies insufficient system transparency and explainability as barriers to developer and deployer accountability, the rule of law and remedies for human-rights violations.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of institutional accountability needs.

facts.quote: The determination remains the subject of ongoing legal dispute
facts.summary: The report explicitly treats the election-annulment example and the role of platform amplification as contested. Its 2023-2024 election examples provide dated background on governance risks, not proof of later events or definitive causal attribution to AI.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific report describing dated, partly contested electoral cases.

facts.quote:
It also requires investments in AI 
capacity, infrastructure, and skills across 
countries and regions, as well as more 
representative data and benchmarks.
facts.summary: The report frames inclusive AI as requiring both representative local data and capacity investment, alongside changes in who develops, defines, owns and governs AI systems.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of inclusion and capacity needs.
